record.provider: Docker Hub (free Personal plan, public repositories)

free_tier.stated: Unlimited public repositories on the free Personal plan; NO documented storage cap on public repositories. Docker's own limits table lists only pull-rate and repository counts, with no storage row. Docker's Feb 2025 policy post says storage-based billing is 'indefinitely delayed' with a promised six-month notice.

retention.stated: Pull count 100 per 6 hours anonymous or 200 per 6 hours authenticated per IP. Large download throughput requires few, large blobs rather than many small ones.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered per-GB; the gate is a pull COUNT, not bytes: 'Unauthenticated users: 100 per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet' and 'Personal (authenticated): 200' per 6 hours. Blobs are served by 307 redirect to a CDN, so one pull can be a multi-GB blob.

record.tooling: oras push / docker push; purpose-built wrapper: github.com/Androsh7/layerstash (chunks >5GB files into ~5GB layers, uploads to Docker Hub or GHCR; author reports 1.8TB personally stored), github.com/xausky/DockerRegisterCloud (654 stars, registry-as-netdisk client with Flutter GUI + direct-download server).
record.chaining: Unlimited public repos per account, and the free account count itself is unlimited. Layer count per repo is not capped, so a single repo holds arbitrarily many blobs; layerstash's <base-tag>-<chunk_n> scheme makes one repo a striped volume of unlimited size.
record.limits_note: Pull count is 100 per 6 hours anonymous or 200 per 6 hours authenticated per IP. No published per-layer size cap, but Docker distribution S3 drivers historically faced issues above 10 GB per layer, recommending shards around 5 GB. Excess request limits return HTTP 429.
record.reliability_note: Storage is unpriced today but Docker reserves the right to add charges and has flip-flopped before (announced Mar 2025, cancelled Apr 2025); the 100-pull/6h IP limit will throttle any fetch fan-out from one host.

evidence.proved: read live: table has columns Pull rate limit / public repos / private repos only; Personal = Unlimited public repos, 200 pulls/6h; no storage row anywhere on the page

read live: 'Storage Charges Delayed Indefinitely ... we have decided to indefinitely delay any storage charges', and 'We did not enforce the Docker Hub rate limit changes previously scheduled for April 1, 2025'

probe: POST -> 401 (anonymous push correctly refused; write requires an account, read does not)

evidence.proved: 'Cloud Sandboxes are pay-as-you-go. We meter compute by the second, and nothing else. A paused sandbox costs nothing. Volumes, egress, and hosting public images and Kits are free.' with sizes from Micro at $0.07 an hour (1 vCPU, 2 GiB) to XL at $1.12 (16 vCPU, 32 GiB)…
